items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1964-11-28
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...I remember that Lesh went in there and got a court order for those, didn't he? [INTERVIEWEE] He got a court order from the estate, yes.

ctx.x: I doubted. I doubted he ever got any money out of them.
Well, getting back to the library, just to bring this thing a little bit into some sort of perspective, I remember that Lesh went in there and got a court order for those, didn't he?
He got a court order from the estate, yes. The estate gave him an order. He gave him an order to take out everything.

items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1964-11-28
items.q: And Jellie was the leader and he arranged the studio arrangements for them... Jazzmen, that he knew like the bunch that was there... didn't need much arrangement for them, but Jellie arranged for them.

ctx.x: That's when he got Bichet with him and Nicholas and De Paris.

But Jellie didn't like De Paris as a trumpet player. He liked him as a player, but he was an obstinate man, I think. He didn't like to be told how to play or why I think. That's the best I can gather from it. Jellie never mentioned his name, but in talking about it later, he says the trumpet player did his best to spoil things or something like that. He said he didn't want to follow instructions, I don't know why.
Well, I guess they figured George Jellie, being the way he was, he came up there, you know. He knew more buzz than any of them and they didn't.
